title: Mornings with Graham & Emmy
teaser: Old plant site bid revives as towns add pauses and protests grow.

lines.text: Good morning and welcome to Mornings with Graham & Emmy, the Michigan Data Wire, your podcast on Michigan's data center buildout. I'm Graham.
And I'm Emmy.
Today we're diving into a developer restarting plans for a big power-hungry facility on an old Emerson Electric campus site.
That one sounds familiar from past talks. What's the latest move?
FOX 2 reports the developer is back at it today, pushing to convert the former plant into a data center.
Why restart now? Is it tied to the AI boom we've seen all summer?
Exactly. The project would add serious new demand on the local grid while raising questions about tax revenue for the community.
Residents nearby would notice changes in electricity rates and how land gets used, right?
That's the core concern. Data centers pull huge amounts of power, and utilities have to plan around that.
How does this fit the bigger pattern we've tracked? We've had pauses in Kalamazoo and Garfield Township just this week.
It does. Those moves came after proposals multiplied fast, and locals wanted time to study grid strain and water use.
So is this Emerson restart likely to face the same pushback?
Probably. The story notes residents will feel impacts on rates and land use, similar to other sites.
What's the history here? Has this site been eyed before?
The summary doesn't give prior details, but restarts like this often follow earlier interest that stalled over permitting.
Who are the main players? The developer, the township, and the utility company?
Yes, and local residents who live close enough to worry about noise or higher bills.
What happens next? Any hearings scheduled soon?
The report doesn't specify dates, but these bids usually go through zoning reviews and public comment periods.
And on the power side, how much demand are we talking? Enough to affect reliability?
Data centers of this scale can add hundreds of megawatts, which is why towns are studying it carefully.
Water use is another big one. Do we know if this site would need cooling water?
The FOX 2 piece flags land use and rates, but water is a common issue statewide right now.
Tax revenue questions too. Would the township gain or lose if it goes through?
That's the trade-off communities weigh. Jobs and taxes versus higher utility costs for everyone.
Sounds like a classic case of balancing growth with local impacts.
It is. We'll keep watching how this one develops alongside the other proposals.
Shifting to quick hits now. Mason County broke ground on two major centers yesterday.
Right. Western Mason County approved construction that will pull significant electricity and create construction jobs.
Locals there will see effects on power reliability and tax revenue, per DC News Now.
Next, Kalamazoo added a moratorium to its zoning code on Saturday to slow the rush.
FOX 17 says it's a temporary ban while the township studies impacts amid statewide grid and water concerns.
Garfield Township in Grand Traverse County is spending a full year drafting rules, starting Friday.
9and10News reports residents could see limits on power demand, noise, and water before anything advances.
Mid-Michigan got its first look at concrete numbers on power and water demands at a university town hall Friday.
MLive covered that session, where residents within 30 miles heard megawatt and daily water figures.
Lakeshore township used existing zoning Friday to block data centers near homes and wells.
MLive notes nearby west Michigan towns are watching to see if the same rules work for them.
Ypsilanti-area residents plan a protest Saturday over water use at two proposed campuses.
MLive says activists target projects that could draw millions of gallons daily from local wells.
A farm owner is seeking city annexation on Friday to build on rural land, per Crain's Detroit.
That would shift tax revenue and control away from the township if it succeeds.
University of Michigan's new computing center plans drew nuclear weapons concerns on Friday.
Michigan Advance reports Ann Arbor activists want clearer answers on possible military ties.
And Lenox Township residents demanded answers Thursday on hidden plans after learning details through back channels.
ClickOnDetroit covered worries about noise, power strain, and lost farmland in Macomb County.
On deck for meetings, nothing major is listed for today specifically.
Listeners should check their local township boards for any zoning or hearing updates this week.
Full sources and the live map at the Michigan Data Center Tracker.
We're back tomorrow.

episode_title: Emerson Restart Sparks Fresh Power and Land Worries
